endorsements.quote: However, machines should not be allowed to make autonomous decisions on the above aspects.
It is imperative to introduce regulatory frameworks that ensure human agents can overrule and control the machine when necessary (Salloch and Eriksen 2024 ).

unlisted_practices: Use ML-based clinical decision support as discussion prompts to engage doctors and patients as co-reasoners rather than to rank diagnoses and treatment options.
Involve patients as active participants and co-reasoners, not merely consenters, in the human-in-the-loop oversight of AI clinical decision support.
Have physicians explore patients' values and preferences and tailor treatment to them regardless of AI tool recommendations.
Design AI clinical decision support to be sensitive to diverse patient values and to encourage clinicians to recognise the value-laden nature of treatment decisions.
Develop value-sensitive healthcare technology policies, guidelines and regulations that reflect the cultural and ethical worldviews of sub-Saharan Africa and similar contexts.

screen.reason: This is a normative ethics and policy commentary discussing the responsible use of AI in African healthcare, focusing on patient moral agency, shared decision-making, and regulatory frameworks.
